topic.title: Conditional utility of historical action codes
topic.question: Under the frozen inputs, history policy and training protocol, do historical action codes improve click AUC beyond aligned historical item content and task-mask membership in the strongest visible model, at justified parameter and measured runtime cost?
topic.hypothesis: Historical action codes may carry useful feedback beyond item fields and task-mask memberships, but the supplied evidence does not isolate this contribution. Inherit the strongest visible trial unchanged as the utility control. Compare full action use with an action-blind representation and a counts-only replacement while retaining representation capacity, all other fields, event order, task masks, training objectives and exposure. If actions vary within membership strata, permute only historical actions within those strata to preserve action counts and membership associations while testing event alignment; absent variation, record that this contrast is uninformative. Keep host history construction, padding and the unknown target action unchanged. Full-use superiority over replacements would provisionally support conditional utility; equivalence or improvement after removal would undermine it. Counts-only equivalence would favor frequency over alignment, while capacity or optimization differences remain alternative explanations. Measure parameters and local training/inference time, repeat informative comparisons within the authorized protocol, and reserve assessment resources. No mechanism or novelty claim is established by the compact evidence.
